_comment: Every behaviour this tree promises to change at the next major.
A staged flip is a promise made to a user now about a release that has not
happened: `This becomes an error in 6.0.0.` is printed on stderr today by
code that still allows the thing. This file is the register of those
promises; `docs/governance/V6_0_PLAN.md` holds the reasoning, the gate
conditions and the open decisions.
`nodus_gate --flips` checks that this file and `src/` agree, in both
directions. It exists because they did not: five promises lived in src/
while COMPATIBILITY_MODEL.md said three, COMPATIBILITY.md said one, and a
design doc said a fourth had been dropped. The two that went missing were
the two whose issues had been closed -- the staging shipped, the issue
closed, and the flip fell out of every register while the code kept
promising it.
Each site in src/ carries a `# v6-flip: <name>` marker, the same way a
regression test carries `# closes: #N`. Attribution needs it: two of these
flips live in one file and their promise text is nearly identical.
`signal` is not decoration. COMPATIBILITY_MODEL.md 5.1 makes a CLI warning
one of three required deprecation signals, and two entries here do not have
one -- which is a fact about whether the flip may be taken, so it belongs
next to the flip.

unknown-type-name.summary: An unrecognised type name becomes an error instead of meaning `any`
unknown-type-name.signal: ok as of the G2 work -- `nodus check` reports it and `nodus run` now does too, cold and warm, for the entry file and for imports
unknown-type-name.why: One transposed letter disables checking on that annotation forever, and the name is unrecoverable at runtime. Recorded in the parser, which is the only place that sees both the name and the token, and reported by whoever asks.

record-equality.summary: Record `==` becomes structural instead of identity
record-equality.signal: ok -- stderr, once per process, when a comparison whose answer will change actually happens
record-equality.why: Records are the only non-structural value, and the exception has exceptions (datetime and duration compare by value). The 6.0.0 semantics already exist as `structural_eq`; the flip is to delegate to it. Design: docs/design/v6/00-record-equality.md.

concurrent-write.summary: A concurrent state write that loses an update becomes an error
concurrent-write.why: Since #544 the warning fires only when an update was actually lost, so the error can only reject a program that is genuinely wrong. The remedies (`merge: "sum"` / `"append"` to combine, `merge: "any"` for deliberate last-write-wins) predate the flip.

worker-dispatcher.summary: A `worker:` declaration with no registered dispatcher becomes an error
worker-dispatcher.why: DECIDED 2026-09-06 (D1): honour it. The code has promised this since 5.3.0 and docs/design/v6/00-record-equality.md had recorded it as dropped when #492 closed; closing an issue did not retract the promise. A `worker:` declaration is an isolation intent, and running in-process while reporting success is the worst available answer -- the same reasoning that made it a warning rather than a silent no-op. Second-oldest signal in the cohort, so notice is not a blocker.

default-store-sqlite.summary: The default workflow store becomes SQLiteWorkflowStore
default-store-sqlite.signal: ok as of the G2 work -- a StagedFlipWarning, which the CLI unsuppresses and renders as `warning: ...`; it was a plain DeprecationWarning raised outside __main__ and no CLI user had ever seen it
default-store-sqlite.why: The only flip in the cohort that costs state rather than a build: runs in the JSON store are invisible to a SQLite one, so an in-flight waiting run becomes unresumable rather than moving. `nodus workflow migrate-store --to sqlite` is the migration. The signal has to become visible before the flip can be taken -- see #797.
